title: Suspected Spinal Injury
summary: If a neck or back injury is possible, ask the person to keep still and support their head in line. Only move them if they are in danger or you need to open the airway.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} if a spinal injury is possible
when: Neck or back pain after a fall, crash, diving or high-energy impact
Numbness, tingling or weakness in arms or legs
Unable to assess because of alcohol, drugs or distracting injuries

steps.title: Make the scene safe
steps.text: If the area is safe, do not move them. Move them only if they are in immediate danger.

steps.title: Ask them to keep still
steps.text: If they are responsive, tell them not to move their head or neck. Encouraging the person to stay still is often the best support.

steps.title: Support the head
steps.text: If you are trained, kneel behind or beside them and hold their head steady in the position found, in line with the body. Do not pull on the head.

steps.title: Check breathing
steps.text: If they are unresponsive, check breathing. Opening the airway takes priority over a possible neck injury. If they are breathing but you must leave them or they may vomit, roll them into the recovery position keeping the head, neck and body in line (ideally with helpers).

steps.title: Keep warm and monitor
steps.text: Cover them, reassure them and keep checking breathing until help arrives.

warningSigns: Loss of feeling or movement in limbs
Loss of bladder or bowel control
doNot: Do not routinely apply a cervical collar as a first aider
Do not move them unless necessary
Do not let them sit up or walk around
Do not remove a crash or motorcycle helmet unless you need to manage the airway or they are not breathing

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
